A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeoSolver work and contain 30 readable pages, including Appendices A–B. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–30 are identical; differences are confined to page 1.

before.justification: v1 reports original GeoSolver benchmark results, test-time scaling experiments, cross-model evaluations and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, scaling experiments, cross-model evaluations and ablations reported in v1.

M1.justification: GeoPRM construction, token-level training, Process-Aware Tree-GRPO and inference procedures in Section 3 and Appendix A are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training data and six remote-sensing tasks. Dataset coverage in Section 4.1 and Appendix A.5, including Table 8, is identical.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in all benchmark and verification experiments. Table 4 retains the same Self-Consistency, Qwen3-VL-8B, GLM-4.1V, GraphPRM and URSA-8B-RM comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain identical splits, sample sizes, metrics, model configurations, training budgets and inference/search settings.

E4.justification: The alignment and data-component ablations in Tables 5–6, hyperparameter analysis in Table 7, qualitative example in Figure 5 and cross-model analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version reports repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests, and v2 adds no seed or run-count information.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are retained, including Tables 1–7 and 9–12 and Figures 3–7. No result entries, rankings or plotted trends change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, reward formulation, advantage calculations and objectives in Equations (1)–(8) are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about performance, test-time scaling and cross-model generalization. The added code-location sentence does not alter these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning hallucinations, reward hacking, scaling behavior and transferable verification remain unchanged, including Appendix B. No new limitations or applicability qualifications appear.

D1.justification: v1 promises to release datasets, models and code upon publication in the introduction. v2 retains that pledge and adds github.com/minglangL/GeoSolver to the abstract, stating that code 'will be available' there. This adds a specific access location without establishing an actual release; implementation details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, research positioning and the reference list are identical. The added project repository address is not a new cited research work.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one sentence identifying the planned code repository, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. All other prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence slightly changes spacing and text placement on page 1, alongside the updated arXiv stamp. Figures, tables and the layout of pages 2–30 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: Adding a specific repository address makes the promised code easier to locate than v1's generic release pledge, providing a small documentation benefit. The PDFs do not establish that code is available, so this is not evidence of completed reproducibility support. Scientific content and evidence, including both appendices, remain unchanged.
